chunks: From him, from ʿAlī, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about madhy that reaches the garment and sticks to it. He said: He washes it, and he does not perform wudu (ablution).

So the apparent meaning in his saying, ‘He washes it,’ is a form of recommendation. We have already fully covered what relates to this chapter in the larger book, and in what we have mentioned here and earlier in the book there is sufficiency, if Allah wills. And this very narrator has narrated what we mentioned.

key_terms.الثَّوْبَ: the garment or clothing affected by the fluid
key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation; indicating the washing is understood as recommended
key_terms.الْمَذْيِ: pre-seminal fluid discussed here in relation to ritual purity
key_terms.وَلَا يَتَوَضَّأُ: and he does not perform wudu (ablution); no ablution is required
key_terms.يَغْسِلُهُ: he washes it; the garment is to be washed

ai.seo_question: Does madhy on clothing require washing and does it invalidate wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of madhy when it reaches and adheres to a garment. The Imam عليه السلام states that it should be washed, while wudu (ablution) is not required, and the compiler notes that the washing is understood as recommended.
